docs.text: Repository and architecture AeroGrid is one EdgeTX widget. Its panels are modules hosted by that widget, not separate EdgeTX widgets. Use the implementation and tests for exact signatures; plans/ contains design material, not the runtime contract. Find your way around Path Responsibility src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/main.lua EdgeTX entry points, native options, event routing, and task enrollment. src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/lib/ Loading, scheduling, services, geometry, rendering, themes, persistence, and editor. src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/panels/ Panel modules, including diagnostics and the fixed-data theme showcase. src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/layouts/ Shipped layouts. src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/assets/ Runtime editor assets and licenses. tests/unit/ , tests/integration/ Module tests and mocked host/UI tests. tests/support/ Firmware-aware mocks, assertions, and fixture helpers. tests/fixtures/ Deterministic SD card, development layouts, and test-only modules. tools/ Packaging, documentation publishing, captures, videos, and tooling tests. docs/ Website sources and reviewed assets. .vscode/ TX16S profile and build/test tasks. .github/workflows/ CI, documentation, and release workflows. build/ Ignored generated output. Follow a dashboard from disk to display EdgeTX loads main.lua with a zone and native Layout and Theme options. Their stable choice positions are maintained by separate registries under /AEROGRID/ ; do not reorder them. layout_store.lua resolves the selected layout. A saved /AEROGRID/layouts/<name>.yaml overrides its bundled counterpart under /WIDGETS/AeroGrid/layouts/ . A missing layout can fall back to Default . yaml.lua parses the constrained YAML format, layout.lua validates it, and grid.lua maps zero-based placements in the 4 x 4 grid to rectangles. dashboard_loader.lua stages service and panel construction, checks module compatibility, and resolves typed settings. Scheduled callbacks update services and panels. dashboard_lifecycle.lua handles bounded reflow and page replacement; editor_controller.lua coordinates editing, previews, and saved-page adoption. Loading, schema conversion, construction, reflow, and save work are split across callbacks. Page retirement and replacement occur in separate callbacks. Keep these boundaries: a synchronous whole-dashboard operation can exceed the firmware budget or invalidate deferred native objects. Glass shares sampled background brightness through /AEROGRID/cache/backgrounds.yml . This generated cache survives widget updates and can be deleted to regenerate it. lib/package.lua declares package, runtime API, panel API, and layout versions. Runtime modules expose RUNTIME_API ; panels expose apiVersion . Deploy the complete widget directory: these checks do not detect every mixed package. Layout conversion uses adjacent header and panel steps in layout.lua , at most one transition per respective loader/save turn. Unsupported versions or missing transitions are rejected. Loading converts only in memory and reports an upgrade notice; explicit editor Save persists the current schema. Scheduling and callback budgets scheduler.lua is firmware-independent. Flight, host transitions, services, and panels share a fair round-robin ring. Host readiness gates enforce input and lifecycle ordering; transitions can hold service or panel work. The default callback segment has eight nominal 2,000-instruction slots ( CAPACITY and INSTRUCTIONS_PER_SLOT ). A task receives at most eight slots per turn ( SLOTS ). Fixed-cost tasks reserve their declared cost; variable-cost tasks declare a minimum and report consumption. Unused slots become available to later tasks. Unfinished work retains its place across callbacks. A continuation requests another turn after the other tasks have had theirs; it needs no separate opt-in. Pending work can run before its next due time. Return no continuation when work should wait for that time. The model's Pre-release features setting permits up to four additional segments for pending/deferred work in the same callback. It is disabled by default and also requires an explicitly enabled saved setting during startup. native_budget.lua owns the EdgeTX-specific mechanism for running those segments beyond the firmware instruction limit; the scheduler does not. Slots are estimates, not measured instruction limits, and exclude scheduler overhead. Keep normal callbacks within the regression budgets , rather than relying on the pre-release extension to hide excessive work. Shared services own firmware reads Panels subscribe in create , retain read-only live views, and render them. Do not poll firmware independently or mutate service-owned data. Shared subscriptions reuse polling; views can change in place without allocation. Module Responsibility telemetry_service.lua Source resolution, values, units, precision, and link freshness. model_service.lua Identity/image, timers, flight mode, and TX voltage. control_service.lua Trims, channel outputs, switches, GVs, and verified flight-count increments. armed_service.lua Effective model/consumer arm condition over shared Control polls. flight_service.lua Shared flight detection, counting, optional Sticky output, and boundary journal. smart_flight.lua Protocol-identified flight sensors and per-sensor receipt/freshness. navigation_service.lua GPS fix, home/pilot position, distance, and bearing. history_service.lua Bounded recordings, cumulative time, extrema, and flight intervals. services.lua Service environment, subscriptions, and scheduled dispatch. Handle unavailable and stale data explicitly. Zero is a valid telemetry value; link-wide freshness cannot prove that a particular sensor has been received. Local controls remain usable without a receiver. Arm consumers use the shared five-second maximum sample age; unknown/stale arm data is not disarmed. A saved model arm condition overrides consumer fallbacks; an explicit empty condition disables arming. Shared flight tracking The factory-scoped flight broker owns a non-UI Control/Telemetry runtime and optional Smart poller. Widgets enroll its shared tasks, which run at most once per tick. Dashboard declarations must agree; a qualified flight pins its arm, detector settings, and output through completion and cleanup. Counter panels only render the shared result. Consumers use services.flight:state() and :boundaries(afterSequence, epoch) , never the Sticky output as an event bus. The boundary journal retains 64 start/end records. Reconcile journal gaps and epoch changes. Boundary at is the candidate/disarm time; observedAt is its confirmation time, so duration excludes the disarm grace. Smart detection requires supported protocol metadata and per-sensor getSourceValue receipt evidence. Cached values and link-wide freshness do not renew it. Unsupported, ambiguous, or stale inputs fall back to standard detection. Keep qualification and output effects in the broker rather than duplicating them in panels. Chart history History observes completed polls, including unchanged values and intervening extrema. Matching condition/source/options subscriptions share bounded storage. Recording pauses on disarm unless a matching flight remains active, and while any AeroGrid layout editor or Model settings dialog is open. Charts render live pixel columns rather than replaying stored history. Late attachment, resizing, and read-only previews start an empty plot; a service runtime rebuild clears recordings. Compatible previews can be adopted after saving without replacing their subscriptions. Appends, rescaling, drawing, and reset work must fit granted slots; charts refresh at most four times a second. Add or change a panel Start with panels/flight-mode.lua ; lib/panel_host.lua defines the contract. Put a module at panels/<type>.lua , with an id matching that layout type. Declaration or callback Contract id , apiVersion , supportedSpans Identity, compatibility, and supported grid spans. settings Typed fields, defaults, bounds, and choices shared by validation and the editor. refreshInterval Interval in 10 ms ticks; zero or absent means every frame. refreshCost , refreshMinCost Fixed cost of 0-8 slots (default 1), or "variable" with a minimum of 1-8. create(parent, rect, settings, services) Construct objects, subscribe, and return instance state. refresh(instance, creating, slots) Update objects; scheduled calls pass false . Returns next interval (1-6000 ticks, or nil to retain it), continuation, and consumed slots. Variable work must report consumption. finish(instance, creating, slots) Optional variable-cost finishing task with the same results as refresh. Requires finishPending and finishMinCost . finishPending(instance) Whether finishing work is ready; an optional second result sets its next minimum grant. Refresh waits while finishing is pending. update(instance, rect, settings, detailsOnly, placement) Reflow/configuration update; host reflows and editor resizes pass placement as the fifth argument. background(instance, creating, slots) Hidden-dashboard work; variable-cost when backgroundMinCost is declared, otherwise one slot. Returns an ignored first result, continuation, and consumed slots. resetSession(instance, now) Reset session state; second result true requests another bounded reset turn. rebindArming(instance, services) Reconnect arming-dependent subscriptions after a model arm-switch change, keeping existing native objects. Receives the service registry's byId table. event(instance, event) Return true when consumed. destroy(instance) Release panel-owned references. validateSettings(settings, span, config, modelArmed) Cross-field or span-dependent validation, with the effective model arm condition. A lifecycle failure disables the affected panel and reports its error without repeatedly invoking the failed panel. Use supportedSpans = { "any" } only when every in-bounds span renders correctly. Use container-local coordinates and shared geometry, including the top-left menu reservation; never assume a TX16S-sized screen. List settings ( type = "table" ) declare entry fields for the shared drawer. Use itemLabel for singular row names. Do not add a panel-specific settings UI. Use theme.lua and primitives.lua for shared typography, geometry, colors, readings, and LVGL objects. They compose typography.lua , panel_layout.lua , and reading.lua ; tests use tests/support/module_loader.lua to compose the same APIs. Choose stable reading fonts from the widest expected representation. Update a label's backing font with primitives.setFont rather than replacing its persistent callback. Cover settings, absent data, every declared span, reflow, and editor installation. Add a panel reference page and, when needed, a capture recipe . Editor and persistence editor.lua owns drafts; editor_ui.lua and editor_drawer.lua present them. editor_controller.lua coordinates the live dashboard. Settings drawers put Label first when declared, then preserve declaration order. layout_store.lua owns layout resolution, verified saves, and backups; layout_registry.lua maintains choice positions. Save writes under /AEROGRID/layouts/ , never over bundled layouts. New Save as... names need a script restart to enter the native Layout picker. Failed saves preserve drafts. model_settings_store.lua validates and serializes revisioned documents through a replaceable persistence backend. On EdgeTX 2.x, model_settings_sidecar.lua stores /AEROGRID/models/<ID>.yaml , linked by the CH32 name. Reads never write; after the broker accepts settings, filename changes fork the record while disarmed. Verified records are installed before claiming CH32, preserving all channel fields. Saves guard model identity, CH32 name, and revision. Layout saves and previews do not write model settings. Changing the arm condition rebuilds registered dashboards and clears captured homes, while preserving layouts and active-flight completion/cleanup. An eventual EdgeTX 3.0 backend can store the same document in model userData without changing callers; it is not selected or implemented yet. Legacy filename-encoded development records are not imported. env.backend supplies read(filename, backup) , check(info) , and write(filename, text, info, guard, armedCondition) . Reads return text and metadata ( missing , identity token , optional recovered / blocked ); forkOnRename opts into sidecar-style adoption. The store guards the original bytes and filename; the backend guards its identity and installation boundary. A model change or session reset advances the flight epoch. Session reset cancels detection, releases its owned output, and clears dashboard session data in bounded callbacks without replacing subscriptions, objects, or drafts. Counting waits for a fresh disarm observation; persistent flight totals remain.

docs.text: Check out and build AeroGrid is a Lua widget, not a firmware fork. Development builds assemble a simulator SD card; release builds create the installable ZIP. Neither requires building EdgeTX or connecting a radio. Get the code git clone https://github.com/thomaskistler/aero-grid.git cd aero-grid git switch -c my-change Fork and clone your fork if you do not have write access. Run guide commands from the repository root. Prerequisites Use macOS, Linux, or WSL with Git, Make, rsync, and Python 3 with virtual-environment support. CI uses Python 3.11. The Makefile requires a Unix shell and bin/ environment paths. Native Windows Companion can use an SD directory accessible from Windows. make setup make test make setup installs pinned development dependencies into build/venv/ . Make invokes that environment directly; activation is unnecessary. make test also creates it when needed. Install the validation tools Runtime changes also need these executables on PATH : Tool Purpose Version edgetx-luac or Lua 5.3 luac Source/test syntax checks in make check . EdgeTX's compiler or Lua 5.3 . lua-language-server Static diagnostics in make lint . CI uses 3.19.1. stylua Formatting and formatting checks. CI pins 2.5.2. For Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt-get install git make rsync python3 python3-venv lua5.3 make check LUA_COMPILER=luac5.3 For macOS with Homebrew: brew install python rsync lua@5.3 make check LUA_COMPILER="$(brew --prefix lua@5.3)/bin/luac" Install LuaLS and StyLua separately. The VS Code Lua extension alone does not put LuaLS on Make's PATH . make check searches for edgetx-luac , luac5.3 , then luac ; pass LUA_COMPILER explicitly if discovery selects a different Lua version. Build make build This recreates build/sdcard/ from tests/fixtures/sdcard/ , overlays the widget source and development layouts, and removes stale bytecode. There is no transpilation or native compilation of AeroGrid. See Run and test in simulators to use it. Stop the simulator before rebuilding. A build deletes simulator-created state in that image. Back up experiments elsewhere, and never build onto a radio SD card or personal model backup. For a separate image, use make build BUILD_DIR=build/experiment and point the simulator at build/experiment/sdcard/ . BUILD_DIR relocates Make-managed environments and output, but not the capture tools' output . Build an installable package make release-package This writes AeroGrid-<version>.zip and .zip.sha256 to build/release/ , using lib/package.lua . The deterministic source-only package includes runtime code/assets, the license, and the Default , Empty , Diagnostics , and Palette layouts. Development fixtures and bytecode are excluded. Use the ZIP to check the actual installation and upgrade procedure . Packaging does not publish; see Publish a release . Build and preview the documentation make docs make docs-serve These install pinned tools into build/docs-venv/ , strictly build the site at build/docs/ , and serve a live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000 . Stop the preview with Ctrl-C. Markdown lives in docs/ . Add or rename pages in both mkdocs.yml and docs/overrides/toc.html . Site styles live in docs/stylesheets/ ; shared Radio Console styles are in console.css . Builds use checked-in screenshots without launching a simulator. Browser installer assets The installer modules live in docs/javascripts/ : radio-storage.mjs owns connections, radio-installer.mjs handles verified widget replacement, radio-panel.mjs drives the UI, and radio-connection-help.mjs provides help. Automatic installation uses mirrored published stable releases and the rolling dev release, not checkout sources. Dev is opt-in; beta/RC releases are excluded. Only WIDGETS/AeroGrid is replaced. Downloads and installed content are verified, but there is no backup or rollback. To preview with mirrored assets: make docs python3 tools/installer_assets.py --output build/docs/installer python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory build/docs Mirroring requires GitHub access; optional GH_TOKEN stays server-side. Use desktop Chrome or Edge over HTTPS or localhost. make docs-serve does not mirror assets; unmirrored releases cannot be installed automatically. Never direct generated output at a radio SD card. Command reference Command Result make help List supported targets. make setup Install development Python dependencies. make test Run Python runner tests and Lua behavior suites. make test-installer Run Python/Node browser-installer tests. make check Run behavior tests and Lua syntax checks. make lint Run LuaLS diagnostics. make format Rewrite source/test Lua with StyLua. make build Recreate the simulator SD image. make capture-setup / make video-setup Install optional image/video dependencies. make release-package Create the installation ZIP and checksum. make docs / make docs-serve Build / preview the website. make clean Delete the configured build directory, including environments and simulator state.

docs.text: make build This recreates build/sdcard/ from tests/fixtures/sdcard/ , overlays the widget source and development layouts, and removes stale bytecode. There is no transpilation or native compilation of AeroGrid. See Run and test in simulators to use it. Stop the simulator before rebuilding. A build deletes simulator-created state in that image. Back up experiments elsewhere, and never build onto a radio SD card or personal model backup. For a separate image, use make build BUILD_DIR=build/experiment and point the simulator at build/experiment/sdcard/ . BUILD_DIR relocates Make-managed environments and output, but not the capture tools' output .

docs.text: make release-package This writes AeroGrid-<version>.zip and .zip.sha256 to build/release/ , using lib/package.lua . The deterministic source-only package includes runtime code/assets, the license, and the Default , Empty , Diagnostics , and Palette layouts. Development fixtures and bytecode are excluded. Use the ZIP to check the actual installation and upgrade procedure . Packaging does not publish; see Publish a release .

docs.text: Issues, changes, and releases Start code work with Check out and build . A development environment is not required to file an issue. File an issue Search existing issues , then open an issue if needed. For bugs, include: Detail What to provide Versions AeroGrid version/commit, EdgeTX version, radio, and display size. Environment Hardware, Dev Kit/WASM, Companion, or mock tests; relevant tool version and OS. Reproduction Minimal steps, model/layout/theme, source setup, and switch/link state. Expected / actual Intended result, observed result, and exact error text. Evidence Logs, screenshots, failing output, or recording; duration and measurements for CPU/memory issues. Attach a minimal layout, not a personal SD card. Remove private model data and GPS coordinates. State whether a fresh build/restart reproduces the failure. For features, describe the problem, workflow, desired behavior, and relevant radio/panel constraints. Discuss large behavioral changes before implementation. Prepare a focused change Base your branch or fork on current main . Keep implementation, regression tests, and directly related documentation together. Lua code and tests use SPDX GPL-2.0-only headers. Element Convention Library modules and test filenames snake_case; tests start with test_ . Panel filenames, IDs, and layout types Matching kebab-case names. Lua locals, functions, fields, settings camelCase. Constants UPPER_SNAKE_CASE ; keep internal constants local. LuaDoc Parameters in signature order, then returns. Comments and documentation describe current contracts and constraints, not historical bug narratives or experiment results. Reuse shared service, rendering, and settings conventions. Cover absent data and boundaries. UI changes also need span/reflow coverage, menu reservation, and editor behavior. See Test and debug and Repository and architecture . Maintain simulator fixtures tests/fixtures/sdcard/ is deterministic input, not a running simulator's SD card. Stop the simulator before deliberately updating tracked fixture files. Shared sensors, mixes, timers, and model setup come from MODELS/model1.yml . Keep registry order stable because widget options store its indices. When manually changing RADIO/radio.yml model selection, keep manuallyEdited: 1 . It covers the exact bytes after that line. Model generation does not update radio settings. Check fixture changes with a fresh make build . Do not commit generated bytecode, environments, simulator state, logs, or incidental captures. Publish only reviewed documentation assets with matching provenance. Check and submit For runtime Lua changes: make format make check make lint stylua --check src/WIDGETS tests make build Inspect formatting changes. Run the relevant tooling tests for tool changes and make docs for documentation. Exercise UI/behavior changes in a simulator. Open a pull request against main explaining the problem, behavior change, regression coverage, and remaining limitations. Link the issue; use Fixes #<number> when appropriate. Content/layouts are version-specific, while navigation, installer UI, and analytics configuration use the current publishing implementation. Snapshots are stored on gh-pages ; do not edit it manually. Repository Settings > Pages > Source must be GitHub Actions .

docs.text: Run and test in simulators Use VS Code for an integrated edit/run loop and Companion for native firmware UI and controls. Record the simulator and version when reporting results. Simulator What you need Best use VS Code EdgeTX Dev Kit VS Code and the Dev Kit extension; first launch downloads WASM firmware. Editor-integrated runs, watch mode, controls, synthetic telemetry, and logs. EdgeTX Simulator supplied with Companion EdgeTX Companion 2.12 with the TX16S simulator. Native UI/control checks, telemetry simulation, and debugging without VS Code. Neither proves receiver behavior, native radio memory stability, or support for every color radio. Prepare a disposable SD image make build Use the absolute path to build/sdcard/ , not src/ , WIDGETS/ , or tests/fixtures/sdcard/ , as the simulator SD-card root. It contains RADIO/ , MODELS/ , IMAGES/ , AEROGRID/ , and WIDGETS/ . Do not run both simulators against the same image at the same time. They can write files on the simulated SD card. Stop the simulator before rebuilding, back up experiments elsewhere, and remember that make build resets them. Use make build BUILD_DIR=build/companion and point Companion at build/companion/sdcard/ if you want separate state. VS Code: EdgeTX Dev Kit Install EdgeTX Dev Kit ( jeffreychix.edgetx-dev-kit ) from VS Code's Extensions view. Use the extension's 2.x simulator commands; Companion is not required. Open the repository folder in VS Code. Open src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/main.lua . In the Command Palette, run EdgeTX: Toggle EdgeTX Mode if it is not already active. Confirm the profile is tx16s , 2.12 , color , 480 x 272 , as recorded in .vscode/edgetx.json . If the profile is missing or stale, run EdgeTX: Set Radio Profile . In workspace settings, set EdgeTX: SD Card Path ( edgetx.sdCardPath ) to the absolute generated image path. Run Tasks: Run Task > AeroGrid: Build Simulator SD , or make build in a terminal. The other supplied task, AeroGrid: Test , runs make test . Run EdgeTX: Open Simulator to boot the fixture and inspect its configured models/screens. Allow the initial firmware download to finish. Use Show Controls for switches, sticks, trims, and radio buttons. To launch the active entry point directly, use EdgeTX: Simulate Script . main.lua includes the App-mode simulation annotation ---@simulate Layout1x1AM zone=0 . For the fixture's existing model/screen configuration, prefer Open Simulator rather than relying on script auto-placement. Companion: native EdgeTX Simulator Install EdgeTX Companion 2.12 for your OS, including the TX16S simulator. There are two launch paths: Companion's embedded simulator, available on macOS too, and the standalone EdgeTX Simulator distributed on Windows/Linux. Launch from Companion Open Companion and create/select a radio profile for RadioMaster TX16S . In Edit Settings... , set that profile's SD Structure path to the absolute generated build/sdcard/ directory. Choose File > Read Models and Settings from SD Path . This opens the fixture's radio settings and models in a Companion document without a connected radio. Confirm that the AeroGrid fixture models are present. Use the document's Simulate Radio action ( Alt+Shift+S ) to boot the complete radio. Use Simulate Model ( Alt+S ) if you intentionally want only the selected model. The embedded simulator uses the profile's SD path for widget/layout/image files, but a temporary copy of the document's radio/model data. Do not expect model changes made during this simulation to be written back to the fixture or Companion document. AeroGrid's user layouts are separate SD-card files; treat that SD path as writable. After rebuilding the image, close the simulation and read models/settings from SD Path again before simulating, so an older open document cannot reintroduce stale model configuration. Launch the standalone simulator On Windows/Linux, open the EdgeTX Simulator installed with Companion ( simulator.exe on Windows; packaged executable naming can vary on Linux). Create the TX16S radio profile in Companion first, then configure the standalone simulator's Startup Options : Option Value Radio Profile Your TX16S profile. Radio Type RadioMaster TX16S. Simulator The available TX16S simulator matching that profile. Data Source SD Path . SD Image Path The absolute path to the generated build/sdcard/ . Click OK . SD Path makes the simulator load radio/model data from the same image that contains the widget. Do not select a default/new .etx data file: that boots a different model configuration. If using Folder instead, set Data Folder and SD Image Path to that same SD-card root, not its MODELS/ subdirectory. The image contains RADIO/radio.yml and MODELS/model*.yml ; the standalone simulator loads these directly and persists radio/model changes. You do not need to import them individually or read a connected radio. If no simulator is listed, check the installed Companion package and profile before modifying the fixture. Use the fixture models A clean build selects AG Overview , with Default on its first screen. Change models with the simulated radio's model-selection UI, just as on a radio. Model What to exercise AG Overview ( model1.yml ) Default; sim; sim2. AG Flight ( model2.yml ) review-model-identity; review-flight-mode; review-flight-timer; review-flight-counter; review-chart. AG Power-Link ( model3.yml ) review-rx-battery; review-cell-sources; review-tx-battery; review-link-status; review-metric. AG Navigation ( model4.yml ) review-navigation. AG Controls ( model5.yml ) review-output; review-trim-panel. AG System ( model6.yml ) Diagnostics; services; services2; review-state; states; Palette; Empty. Review and simulator-only layouts live in tests/fixtures/layouts/development/ ; make build adds them to the disposable simulator image without including them in the widget source or release ZIP. All screens use App mode and Modern Dark. Models share sensors, switches, mixes, trims, and timer setup, but EdgeTX keeps live timer/trim state per model. Useful scenarios: Layout/model Inputs and purpose sim / sim2 Telemetry / radio-local values and metric modes. State ( review-state ) SF changes MODE, SA changes RATE, SB changes FLAP. NO MIDDLE intentionally leaves SA's middle position unmapped. Palette Telemetry-free theme samples; change Theme or add a custom theme . Diagnostics / services / services2 Host errors and service-probe views. AG Flight SF down arms; CH3 above 25% with live telemetry exercises detection. Start/end windows are ten seconds; Smart detection is enabled. AG Flight reserves Sticky L01 for flight status. Its one-shot agstart and agend tracks play three tones at flight start and four at end, not at model startup. The flight-counter screen reads the shared model count. To change the baseline, follow Maintain simulator fixtures .

docs.text: Test and debug Start with the smallest test covering the change. Mocks validate logic, simulators validate firmware UI, and radios validate hardware behavior; none replaces the others. Run the automated Lua suites make test make check make test checks menu artwork and the Python runner, then runs every test_*.lua under tests/ , excluding support modules. Each suite gets a fresh Lua 5.3 runtime and the repository root as its chunk argument. The runner stops at the first failure and prints its captured AeroGrid errors and traceback. Tests must be ASCII. The runner removes the string metatable to resemble EdgeTX: use string.sub(value, ...) , not value:sub(...) . The desktop runtime does not reproduce radio integer/float widths or native resource behavior. make check also parses source/test Lua with an EdgeTX or Lua 5.3 compiler. Install the validation tools , or pass: make check LUA_COMPILER=/absolute/path/to/edgetx-luac Choose the right test layer Change Start here Layout parsing, validation, geometry, persistence Corresponding tests/unit/lib/ suites. Source resolution or service data Corresponding service suites in tests/unit/lib/ . Panel settings/presentation tests/unit/panels/ and tests/integration/widget/test_*_review.lua . Loading, scheduling, callback budgets Focused test_catalog_loading.lua , test_host_faults.lua , test_callback_budget.lua , and widget queue/slot suites. Editor commands/dialogs test_editor.lua , test_editor_ui.lua , and test_panel_installation.lua . Arming, flight detection, model settings, reset Shared-arming/shared-flight, model-settings, and session-reset suites. Reflow or resource lifetime Rendered-geometry, all-panel-spans, panel-reflow, font-callback, and resource-stability suites. Use tests/support/runtime_fixture.lua for runtime helpers without LVGL, widget_fixture.lua for a mocked host, and edgetx.lua for firmware behavior and LVGL inspection. Firmware-dependent mocks require implementation citations; do not make a mock agree with an unverified assumption. Performance and resource regressions tests/integration/widget/test_callback_budget.lua measures callback instructions across loading, dense layouts, services, and reflow. Its ceiling is below 15,000, leaving headroom against EdgeTX's 20,000-instruction limit. Focused suites add their own budgets; these are mock measurements, not hardware timing guarantees. Resource suites check reload collection, retained Lua memory, LVGL object counts, sustained output updates, and font callbacks. They do not measure native bitmap/LVGL memory or firmware GC cadence. Chart tests cover functional behavior; evaluate responsiveness on a radio. On macOS with Companion 2.12, measure Model and panel drawer construction: python3 tools/measure-model-settings.py python3 tools/measure-model-settings.py --mode callbacks --output build/model-settings-callbacks.json python3 tools/measure-panel-settings.py python3 tools/measure-panel-settings.py --mode callbacks --output build/panel-settings-callbacks.json Reports include per-row grants and native instruction bounds with firmware property polling. Callback mode includes scheduler/host work and rejects usage reaching 15,000 instructions. Neither mode establishes physical-radio timing or safety; mock regression envelopes remain separate from production grants. Both drawers use lib/settings_ui.lua . Model construction reserves 14 slots: one per step except two for the logical-switch list. Panel rows reserve one slot and can share callbacks; lifecycle operations retain full grants and dialog opening/replacement/closing boundaries. The panel profiler covers every catalog panel, maximum-size lists, nested editors and conditional rows. Browser installer tests Use Python's standard library and Node.js 22: make test-installer Tests cover release mirroring, connections, confirmation, integrity, and preservation of non-widget files. Never use a real radio for automated destructive tests. For an optional rendered check, install Playwright/Chromium separately and serve a built site with mirrored assets : node tests/browser/radio-panel.smoke.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8000/ It needs two available mirrored stable releases and uses disposable browser storage, not a radio or the OS folder picker. Optional environment variables are PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE (external index.mjs path), PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL=chrome , and INSTALLER_KEYBOARD=1 for keyboard activation. Python tooling tests Run the suites relevant to the changed tool; make test does not run these. Release packaging (standard library): python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_release_*.py' Menu icon and tile artwork checks also use only the standard library: make test-artwork They run as part of make test / make check , including CI. docs.text: Project tools Native capture tools create documentation images from Companion's TX16S simulator library. They use isolated widget/SD copies, not src/ or the active development image. Outputs stay in ignored build/ directories until reviewed. For recordings and narration, see Tutorial videos . Capture documentation images with native firmware Requirements: macOS , EdgeTX Companion 2.12, and Xcode command-line tools ( clang++ , lipo ). The simulator library must be single-architecture; Intel firmware on Apple Silicon needs Rosetta. The default application is /Applications/EdgeTX Companion 2.12.app ; override it with --companion "/path/to/Companion.app" . These tools do not run in CI. Panel screenshots make capture-setup build/capture-venv/bin/python tools/capture-panels.py --panel trim-panel build/capture-venv/bin/python tools/capture-panels.py --all Select one of --panel <type> , --recipe <path> , or --all . The setup target installs pinned PyYAML. Bundled recipes cover user-facing panels, Host diagnostics, and Service probe. Outputs go to build/doc-capture/<panel>/ : gallery crops, full-frame.png , frame.rgb565 , recipe.yaml , provenance.json , sdcard/ , and simulator.log . Regeneration replaces that panel's output. --all runs sequentially; failure keeps diagnostics and any completed panels, but never publishes assets. Defaults are 480 x 272, Modern Dark, App mode, unscaled crops, and a 10-pixel border. Recipes control samples and readiness checks. Synthetic inputs pass through real services/panels; the images show firmware rendering, not receiver telemetry validation. Change a capture recipe Copy a recipe from tools/capture-recipes/ and run it explicitly: build/capture-venv/bin/python tools/capture-panels.py --recipe /path/to/example.yaml Recipes specify panel , theme , border , named panels placements/config, and sample . Placements are zero-based in the 4 x 4 grid, cannot overlap, and have row spans of 1 or 2. Span-shaped image names must match their dimensions. Use bundled recipes for supported sample fields, sensor units, and precision; every configured source needs a sample. tools/capture_recipes.py owns validation, model setup, input adapters, and readiness. capture-panels.py prepares, captures, crops, and records provenance. Add adapters here, not capture-specific behavior in production modules. Variants under tools/capture-recipes/variants/ require --recipe . The Host diagnostics scheduler variant accepts uncropped companions panels; publish its crop/provenance as scheduler-2x2.png and scheduler-provenance.json . Disclose capture-only presentation changes, notably brighten_supporting_text: true and the timer's hide_bottom_bar: true . Production config.visual: none is not a capture override. Model-image paths are recipe-relative and need firmware-safe PNG names; verify redistribution rights before publishing. Capture hooks patch only isolated copies: synthetic panel inputs enter through dashboard_loader.lua , editor activation uses context.editorController.openEditor , and readiness wraps the refresh export. Keep those hooks aligned with runtime boundaries. Run capture tests and inspect frames/provenance. Editor and setup screenshots build/capture-venv/bin/python tools/capture-editor.py --scene select-layout build/capture-venv/bin/python tools/capture-editor.py --scene chart-settings build/capture-venv/bin/python tools/capture-editor.py --scene navigation-location Use --help for scene names. Omitting --scene captures the default editor/setup set; dashboard, theme, and model-menu scenes are opt-in. Panel drawers use the capture recipes and need make capture-setup . Inputs use native touch/key actions or production editor commands in the isolated copy. Each scene writes its PNG, SD card, framebuffer, and log under build/editor-capture/<scene>/ . Selected directories are replaced; the root provenance.json describes only that invocation. Tall settings drawers are stitched from captures with leading rows hidden in the isolated copy, not scrolled screenshots. The tool removes the scrollbar; review the resulting image before publication. navigation-location captures the location overlay and its frozen QR code. Full dashboard screenshot build/capture-venv/bin/python tools/capture-editor.py --scene dashboard This captures the full display with Default and Modern Dark , without color/presentation overrides or an open editor. It uses fixture model data and synthetic telemetry through real services. Readiness checks cover all nine panels and their primary readings. Outputs are under build/editor-capture/dashboard/ , with inputs/hashes in the root provenance. Theme samples use --scene theme-modern-dark , theme-modern-light , or theme-custom ; panel recipes also accept theme: modern-light . Publish reviewed images Review the full frame, crops, sample disclosures, and provenance, then copy only intended PNGs and matching provenance: Asset Destination Panel galleries docs/assets/panels/<panel>/ Editor/setup captures docs/assets/editor/ Full dashboard shared by README/home docs/assets/dashboard/ Theme samples docs/assets/theme/ Keep captions consistent with synthetic inputs and overrides. Do not use single-scene provenance to describe unrelated captures. Leave SD cards, logs, raw frames, and incidental images in build/ . Run make docs after publishing. Package a release deterministically See Build an installable package for the command and contents. tools/package-release.py enforces explicit runtime allowlists, required layouts/assets, and symlink rejection. Use --version-only to print the version or --output <directory> to relocate the ZIP/checksum. Run the packaging tests when changing it.

docs.text: Record and recreate tutorial videos tools/video.py records native TX16S interactions, uses cached Microsoft Cora narration, and composites with FFmpeg. It is local-only and does not upload. Recipes/actions live in tools/video-recipes/ ; generated media, SD cards, caches, and provenance stay in ignored build/video/ . Install and run make video-setup build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py --help build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py validate build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py capture Setup installs pinned imageio-ffmpeg , including its encoder. Native capture also requires macOS, Xcode command-line tools, and Companion 2.12. The default library is: /Applications/EdgeTX Companion 2.12.app/Contents/Resources/libedgetx-tx16s-simulator.dylib Override with --library ; universal libraries also need --architecture arm64 or --architecture x86_64 . Intel firmware on Apple Silicon requires Rosetta. Rendering and speech caching do not require Companion. The default recipe is add-move-resize-panel.json . Pass --recipe tools/video-recipes/<name>.json on each command for another tutorial. --output overrides build/video/<recipe-id>/ . compile builds the recorder; prepare creates the SD card; capture does both and records. Preparation refuses an existing SD card, so use a new output directory for another capture. Capture uses current widget sources, including uncommitted changes, in an isolated copy. Touch/key scripts operate the firmware UI. The editing recipe injects demonstration telemetry only into that copy; it does not validate receiver telemetry. Narration without storing credentials speech is offline by default. Clips are keyed by text, voice, rate, and PCM format. Text/rate changes need new clips; timing changes can reuse them. WAVs must be intact 48 kHz, 16-bit mono PCM and fit their slots with 0.3 seconds to spare. Shorten text, increase recipe rate, or adjust timing if a clip fails. The tool does not truncate or automatically accelerate audio. Paid Azure synthesis requires explicit opt-in: # Set AZURE_SPEECH_KEY securely in your environment, never in tracked files. export AZURE_SPEECH_REGION=westus2 build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py speech --online unset AZURE_SPEECH_KEY AZURE_SPEECH_REGION This sends narration text to Azure and can incur charges. It uses en-US-CoraMultilingualNeural and reuses valid cached clips. Never put credentials in recipes, arguments, or shell history. --cache selects another ignored cache directory. speech --cache-source /path/to/clips imports recipe legacy_cache filenames: format/duration are checked, but you must listen to verify their content/rate. Render and inspect # Offline screen-only excerpt: build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py render --silent --limit 12 # Photo composite with cached narration: build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py render --photo /path/to/tx16s.webp # Review selected rendered-timeline frames: build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py frames --times 0,7.3,21.3,42.1 render never synthesizes speech. --silent bypasses speech requirements; --limit renders an excerpt. Omit --photo for a 480 x 272 screen-only video without physical-button feedback. --raw accepts an external recording. Re-rendering replaces output files. Photo geometry is configured for a user-supplied 4000 x 4000 image based on the RadioMaster TX16S product photograph . The tool neither supplies nor downloads/upscales it. Verify usage rights and retain RadioMaster attribution; the repository GPL does not license the photo. Other images need matching crop, screen, and mask geometry. Output Purpose frames.rgb565 , last-frame.png , simulator.log Raw recording and diagnostics. frame-*.png , frames-sheet.png Frame review. sdcard/ , video-native Isolated fixture and recorder. feedback.mov , radio.png , bezel.png Regenerable composite intermediates. <recipe-id>.mp4 , transcript.txt Video and narration transcript. capture-provenance.json , render-provenance.json Inputs/hashes, disclosures, and verification limits. Recordings are RGB565 little-endian, 480 x 272, 20 fps. Rendering removes trim_start and holds the last frame when needed; provenance records the hold. Capture checks that timeline touches reached firmware, not that navigation succeeded. External raw recordings have no reconstructed capture provenance. Watch the complete result for navigation, save behavior, voice alignment, units, and photo placement before publishing. Recipe format and reproducibility Use a bundled JSON recipe as the schema example. Version 1 rejects unknown fields and requires initial state, timing, action path, narration, radio geometry, and provenance. Actions are recipe-relative tick x y down rows with 10 ms ticks; negative x encodes key -x-1 ( -2 is RTN). Consecutive touch-down positions form a drag; end with release and do not overlap contacts. The bundled tutorials cover: Recipe Demonstrated scope create-empty-dashboard Add an App-mode widget with Empty and Modern Dark. add-move-resize-panel Configure, move, resize, and save a panel. Restart/layout selection are narrated, not replayed. model-settings Arm/detection settings, Sticky L01 with start sound, flight-status output, and session reset. The end sound is narrated, not replayed. Fixed-coordinate scripts depend on firmware, widget behavior, and machine load. There is no UI-state recovery: maintain the scripts and retain approved videos separately rather than assuming byte-identical recreation. Validate changes build/video-venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_video.py' Tests cover validation, source isolation, cache behavior, mocked synthesis, and offline screen/photo render-and-decode checks. Native capture needs separate local review. Tests must never require paid speech.

docs.text: Flight counter 1x2 2x1 2x2 Displays the model's selected flight total and highlights an AeroGrid-detected active flight. Flight tracking is shared by AeroGrid dashboards and does not require a visible Flight counter. Settings Setting Default What it does Label FLT Panel heading. Clear it to restore the default. Configure arming, detection, optional sounds, and Flight count source in Model settings . Those settings apply across the model's dashboards; this panel only configures its label. External values are read from flight mode 0 and never written. AeroGrid keeps its own count regardless of the displayed source; the totals can differ because flight detection is independent. Continuous disarming for the configured end window does; rearming within that window keeps the same flight open. An unavailable arm reading cannot confirm disarming. If dashboard arm conditions conflict or settings change during a flight, the current flight finishes using its original condition and output. New flights wait until the configuration is consistent. The Session reset switch cancels detection and clears its output without changing flight totals. Disarm before another flight can be counted. AeroGrid does not write flight CSV files. AeroGrid supports totals up to 16,777,215. Its total persists through transmitter restarts, but in-flight detection state does not. Changing model or restarting during a flight can lose its history and qualify it again. States Condition Presentation Resting or qualifying Count and normal styling, without a badge. docs.text: Navigation 1x2 2x1 2x2 Shows distance from home and the north-up bearing from home toward the model, with optional GPS coordinates and satellite count. Bearing is not aircraft heading, transmitter orientation, or a return-home instruction. Settings Setting Default What it does Label NAV Panel heading. GPS source GPS EdgeTX GPS source supplying the model's coordinates. It must return a coordinate table. Home position edgetx edgetx uses EdgeTX home; first-arm captures home using the effective armed condition. Satellite count source Not set Optional source reporting a plain nonnegative integer count of locked satellites, not a packed GPS-status value. Warn below satellites 8 Warns when the satellite count is strictly below this value. Nonnegative integers, steps of 1. Requires Satellite count source . Critical below satellites 4 Critical alarm when the satellite count is strictly below this value. Nonnegative integers, steps of 1; must not exceed Warn below satellites . Requires Satellite count source . Show tape off Replaces bearing text with a scrolling direction tape where space permits. Bearing format degrees degrees shows numeric azimuth; quadrant shows notation such as N29°E . Shown only when Show tape is off. Show coordinates off Shows the model's latitude and longitude where space permits, independently of Show tape . Show satellites on Shows the satellite icon and locked-satellite count in the header where space permits. Requires Satellite count source ; turning it off does not disable satellite alerts. Accent cyan Normal panel accent. Behavior Distance from home is always the main reading. It uses metres or kilometres according to distance. Zero latitude and longitude together mean no fix, matching EdgeTX's uninitialized GPS values. A valid 0m reading means the model is at home, not that GPS is unavailable. Satellite count and alerts With Satellite count source selected, Show satellites controls the satellite icon and locked-satellite count in the header. It defaults to on, including for existing layouts without this setting. Turning it off hides both the icon and count, not the warning, critical, missing-source, or stale indications. The indicator is also hidden when it cannot fit; alerts remain active. With no source selected, neither the indicator nor satellite alerts appear. The defaults make 0 critical, 4 warning, and 8 normal. Thresholds do not control home capture, and distance never triggers an alarm. First-arm home With Home position set to edgetx , home comes from EdgeTX. Selecting first-arm captures a separate AeroGrid home without changing EdgeTX home or the flight controller's return-home position. It uses Arm switch in AeroGrid → Model settings . Saving None disables first-arm capture. For legacy switches, see Older layouts . AeroGrid must observe disarmed, then armed; opening the widget already armed does not capture home. With an effective armed switch, AeroGrid captures the home position when the model is first armed. If that capture fails, each later disarm and re-arm tries again until home is set. A captured home or failed attempt survives telemetry loss, panel recreation, and layout or theme reloads in this widget instance. Panels using the same GPS source and armed switch share the capture. A different pair has its own capture. Home is not saved to disk: restarting the radio, reloading the model, or removing and recreating the widget starts a new session. Separate widget instances have independent homes. Changing the model's Arm switch clears retained AeroGrid homes on every dashboard. The Session reset switch also clears these homes; observe a new disarm/arm transition to capture again. EdgeTX home is unchanged. If HOME NOT SET appears, check for a live GPS fix before disarming and rearming. Capture requires a recent position; later GPS recovery alone does not capture home. To investigate further, enable Host diagnostics → log before repeating the attempt, then tap that panel in widget fullscreen to read the outcome. Bearing display Show tape places the tape below distance in square and tall panels, and beside it in wide panels. Compass directions scroll beneath a fixed pointer. When bearing is unavailable, the tape shows the reason instead of a pointer and scale that could imply due north. With Show tape off, Bearing format selects numeric azimuth or quadrant notation. Bearing text and Show coordinates are displayed only where they fit; a tape that cannot fit yields to distance. Stale data retains the last bearing with the panel's STALE indication. The code and coordinates are frozen when opened; close and reopen for a newer position. A stale fix is marked LAST KNOWN POSITION . Without a valid position, tapping does nothing. Tap anywhere or press RTN (Back/Exit on other radios) to return. Location details are unavailable outside widget fullscreen and while editing. The radio generates the QR code without a network connection; following it on a phone uses Google Maps. docs.text: YAML reference Use this reference to write layout YAML by hand or with an AI agent. For on-radio settings and behavior, see the panel reference . For custom palettes, see Theme files . File locations AeroGrid reads YAML layout files from two places: Bundled layouts: /WIDGETS/AeroGrid/layouts/<name>.yaml . User layouts: /AEROGRID/layouts/<name>.yaml (on the SD card). A user layout with the selected name takes precedence over a bundled layout of the same name. The user folder is outside the widget folder, so a widget update does not replace user layouts. The editor accepts names of 1–24 letters, digits, _ or - ; Empty is reserved for the blank screen. Use that name as the filename stem. If loading a candidate fails, AeroGrid can try its backup, the bundled file of that name, then the bundled default and its backup. Document structure A new layout should use version 5 and exactly a 4 × 4 grid. col and row are zero-based; spans count grid cells. The cell at the upper left is (0, 0) . Top-level key Type Required Meaning version integer yes Layout schema version. Write 5 . grid mapping yes Must contain columns: 4 and rows: 4 . Other grid dimensions are rejected. panels sequence of mappings yes Ordered panel placements. Use [] for an empty layout. session mapping no Legacy compatibility only; see Session . theme mapping no Not supported. A layout that has this key is reported as invalid. Choose a theme in widget settings instead. Each panels entry has these placement keys: Key Type Required Rule id string yes Unique within the layout; letters, digits, _ and - only ( ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ). type string yes Panel kind, using the exact names in the Panels sections below. It must also contain only letters, digits, _ and - . col integer yes Starting column, 0–3. row integer yes Starting row, 0–3. colSpan integer yes Positive width in cells; must fit within column 4 and be supported by the panel. rowSpan integer yes Positive height in cells; must fit within row 4 and be supported by the panel. config mapping no Panel-specific settings. Omit it to use panel defaults; otherwise write a mapping, not a sequence or scalar. A placement must fit the 4 × 4 grid: col + colSpan <= 4 and row + rowSpan <= 4 . Placements may touch edges but may not occupy the same cell. If two placements overlap, the first valid placement in the sequence wins and the later one is dropped. A panel must also support its exact span, written as <colSpan>x<rowSpan> (for example, 2x1 ); the word any in a panel's span list accepts every in-bounds span. Panel IDs and types are case-sensitive. Unknown top-level keys and extra placement keys are preserved rather than rejected. In contrast, a key inside config that the panel does not declare is reported as an unknown setting; spelling and case must match exactly. Session session is optional and must be a mapping when present. Its only declared key is armSource ; unknown session keys are not reported and are not retained in the normalized session: Key Type Default Meaning armSource string unset Accepted so existing layouts load, but no longer used. Configure Arm switch in Model settings instead. Configure arming, session reset, and flight detection/output in Model settings , not layout YAML. For compatibility behavior, see Older layouts . Custom State conditions remain independent. Validation and errors The loader parses and validates a candidate before building panels. Unsupported YAML syntax, an unsupported schema version, a missing or non-4×4 grid, a non-sequence panels value, or the unsupported layout-level theme key makes the candidate invalid; AeroGrid reports the load problem and may recover using the next backup or bundled candidate. Versions 1–4 are migrated to version 5 in memory. Existing panel, Navigation, and legacy arm settings are retained. Version 4 detection settings remain available for migration to Model settings. Save writes version 5 without deleting retained legacy arm conditions. Write version 5 for new files. An invalid panel entry is rejected without preventing other valid entries from loading. This includes a non-mapping entry, an unsafe or duplicate ID, an unknown panel type, invalid placement values, a placement outside the grid, an overlap, or a span the panel does not support. The failed panel is dropped and its reason is reported. When overlaps occur, the earlier accepted entry remains. Missing or wrong-typed panel settings and invalid choice values fall back to their defaults, with a warning where appropriate. Nested entries and cross-field rules receive panel-specific validation. A panel that cannot be constructed is dropped. The editor rejects previews with warnings and refuses to save invalid settings. Numeric bounds and steps are editor constraints unless runtime validation is explicitly noted below. Correct every warning rather than relying on fallback behavior. Unknown config keys are kept in the resolved configuration but reported as “is not a setting of this panel”; they are not silently discarded. This catches typos. A non-mapping config is normalized to an empty mapping, so always use the mapping form. Unknown top-level keys and extra panel-entry keys are retained without a setting warning; do not rely on them having meaning to this version of AeroGrid. YAML parsing and structural validation do not prove that an EdgeTX source exists on a particular model or radio. Use exact source names as the radio reports them. A missing live source can still render as unavailable even when the layout structure is valid. YAML syntax supported The widget uses a deliberately small YAML parser, not a general YAML implementation. Emit only these forms: Indented block mappings ( key: value ) and sequences ( - item ), using two spaces per indentation level . Tabs and odd-space indentation are errors. Strings, numbers, lowercase true and false , and null or ~ scalars. To force a string that looks like a number, boolean, or null, quote it. Single-quoted strings; represent an apostrophe inside one as '' . Double-quoted strings support \\ , \" , \n , \r and \t escapes. Comments beginning with # at the start of a line or after whitespace. A # inside a quoted string is preserved. Empty flow collections only: [] and {} . They are useful for empty sequences and mappings; non-empty inline collections are unsupported. Empty mapping values with indented children, including nested mappings and lists. Do not use anchors or aliases, tags, block scalars ( | or > ), flow-style non-empty lists or maps, merge keys, directives, or other general YAML features. Duplicate mapping keys are rejected. Mapping keys must begin with an ASCII letter or _ , and may then contain letters, digits, _ or - . Quote text that could otherwise be parsed as a boolean, number or null. Prefer double-quoting source names, labels and other strings when uncertain. Panels Omitted settings use their listed defaults. “Unset” means the setting has no schema default and stays unset unless specified. docs.text: AeroGrid reads YAML layout files from two places: Bundled layouts: /WIDGETS/AeroGrid/layouts/<name>.yaml . User layouts: /AEROGRID/layouts/<name>.yaml (on the SD card). A user layout with the selected name takes precedence over a bundled layout of the same name. The user folder is outside the widget folder, so a widget update does not replace user layouts. The editor accepts names of 1–24 letters, digits, _ or - ; Empty is reserved for the blank screen. Use that name as the filename stem. If loading a candidate fails, AeroGrid can try its backup, the bundled file of that name, then the bundled default and its backup.

docs.text: A new layout should use version 5 and exactly a 4 × 4 grid. col and row are zero-based; spans count grid cells. The cell at the upper left is (0, 0) . Top-level key Type Required Meaning version integer yes Layout schema version. Write 5 . grid mapping yes Must contain columns: 4 and rows: 4 . Other grid dimensions are rejected. panels sequence of mappings yes Ordered panel placements. Use [] for an empty layout. session mapping no Legacy compatibility only; see Session . theme mapping no Not supported. A layout that has this key is reported as invalid. Choose a theme in widget settings instead. Each panels entry has these placement keys: Key Type Required Rule id string yes Unique within the layout; letters, digits, _ and - only ( ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ). type string yes Panel kind, using the exact names in the Panels sections below. It must also contain only letters, digits, _ and - . col integer yes Starting column, 0–3. row integer yes Starting row, 0–3. colSpan integer yes Positive width in cells; must fit within column 4 and be supported by the panel. rowSpan integer yes Positive height in cells; must fit within row 4 and be supported by the panel. config mapping no Panel-specific settings. Omit it to use panel defaults; otherwise write a mapping, not a sequence or scalar. A placement must fit the 4 × 4 grid: col + colSpan <= 4 and row + rowSpan <= 4 . Placements may touch edges but may not occupy the same cell. If two placements overlap, the first valid placement in the sequence wins and the later one is dropped. A panel must also support its exact span, written as <colSpan>x<rowSpan> (for example, 2x1 ); the word any in a panel's span list accepts every in-bounds span. Panel IDs and types are case-sensitive. Unknown top-level keys and extra placement keys are preserved rather than rejected. In contrast, a key inside config that the panel does not declare is reported as an unknown setting; spelling and case must match exactly.

docs.text: The loader parses and validates a candidate before building panels. Unsupported YAML syntax, an unsupported schema version, a missing or non-4×4 grid, a non-sequence panels value, or the unsupported layout-level theme key makes the candidate invalid; AeroGrid reports the load problem and may recover using the next backup or bundled candidate. Versions 1–4 are migrated to version 5 in memory. Existing panel, Navigation, and legacy arm settings are retained. Version 4 detection settings remain available for migration to Model settings. Save writes version 5 without deleting retained legacy arm conditions. Write version 5 for new files. An invalid panel entry is rejected without preventing other valid entries from loading. This includes a non-mapping entry, an unsafe or duplicate ID, an unknown panel type, invalid placement values, a placement outside the grid, an overlap, or a span the panel does not support. The failed panel is dropped and its reason is reported. When overlaps occur, the earlier accepted entry remains. Missing or wrong-typed panel settings and invalid choice values fall back to their defaults, with a warning where appropriate. Nested entries and cross-field rules receive panel-specific validation. A panel that cannot be constructed is dropped. The editor rejects previews with warnings and refuses to save invalid settings. Numeric bounds and steps are editor constraints unless runtime validation is explicitly noted below. Correct every warning rather than relying on fallback behavior. Unknown config keys are kept in the resolved configuration but reported as “is not a setting of this panel”; they are not silently discarded. This catches typos. A non-mapping config is normalized to an empty mapping, so always use the mapping form. Unknown top-level keys and extra panel-entry keys are retained without a setting warning; do not rely on them having meaning to this version of AeroGrid. YAML parsing and structural validation do not prove that an EdgeTX source exists on a particular model or radio. Use exact source names as the radio reports them. A missing live source can still render as unavailable even when the layout structure is valid.
docs.title: Validation and errors

docs.text: The widget uses a deliberately small YAML parser, not a general YAML implementation. Emit only these forms: Indented block mappings ( key: value ) and sequences ( - item ), using two spaces per indentation level . Tabs and odd-space indentation are errors. Strings, numbers, lowercase true and false , and null or ~ scalars. To force a string that looks like a number, boolean, or null, quote it. Single-quoted strings; represent an apostrophe inside one as '' . Double-quoted strings support \\ , \" , \n , \r and \t escapes. Comments beginning with # at the start of a line or after whitespace. A # inside a quoted string is preserved. Empty flow collections only: [] and {} . They are useful for empty sequences and mappings; non-empty inline collections are unsupported. Empty mapping values with indented children, including nested mappings and lists. Do not use anchors or aliases, tags, block scalars ( | or > ), flow-style non-empty lists or maps, merge keys, directives, or other general YAML features. Duplicate mapping keys are rejected. Mapping keys must begin with an ASCII letter or _ , and may then contain letters, digits, _ or - . Quote text that could otherwise be parsed as a boolean, number or null. Prefer double-quoting source names, labels and other strings when uncertain.

docs.text: Edit a dashboard on the radio Watch the panel editing walkthrough on YouTube . Add a dashboard first, then customize its panels on the radio. Long-press the dashboard to enter widget fullscreen. An AeroGrid icon appears in the top-left corner. Tap AeroGrid → UI setup to start editing, even on an Empty dashboard. You can also long-press a panel again. Enter also starts editing. A gear icon appears in the top-right corner of each panel. AeroGrid → Model settings opens shared model settings without entering layout edit mode. Changes save automatically, independently of layout Save/Save as... . The host menu is hidden while editing so it does not cover panel resize corners. See Model settings for shared arming, flight detection, flight-status output, and the Session reset switch. Session reset preserves unsaved layout edits and does not close an open Model settings page. Action How Add Tap the + panel , then choose a panel type. Its settings open automatically. Move Drag the panel's body to a free position. Reorder Drag onto another panel. Compatible panels exchange positions or order; other panels stay put. Resize Drag the top-left, bottom-left, or bottom-right corner. The opposite corner stays fixed. Configure Tap the gear in the top-right corner. Remove Open the gear, then choose Remove panel . Removal is immediate. Panels snap to the 4 × 4 layout grid. Moves and sizes must fit without overlapping other panels. The + panel disappears when there is no free cell. There are no grid lines or resize handles: drag the corners directly. Moving and resizing require touch. Configure panels Use the native choices, toggles, number controls, and text keyboard in the settings dialog. Sources, switches, and timers use EdgeTX pickers. Long titles may be shortened or hidden. Widen the panel or use a shorter label. Metric and State entries appear as named rows with a summary of their settings. Tap a row to edit it, or tap the full-width + row to add an entry. In a metric entry, choose Source to change the reading. In a State entry, open a state condition to edit When , Text , and Background . The first true condition wins. Each entry supports up to three conditions; + appends one at the bottom. Delete and recreate a condition to change its priority. Background choices are normal , active , warning , and critical . The main entry's winning choice sets the whole panel's appearance, including its background, sidebar, text colors, and badge. Supporting entries never change the panel mode. Press RTN or tap outside a dialog to return one level. Changes remain in your draft. If settings cannot be previewed, a Panel preview failed message appears. Open its details to read the full panel-specific explanation, then correct the settings. The short status line clears when the preview succeeds. For simulator debugging, see Simulator logs and caught errors . Save or discard changes From the editing dashboard, press RTN . If nothing changed, editing closes. Otherwise choose an action: Action Result Save Updates the current layout and exits editing. Save as... Asks for a name and saves a separate layout. Discard changes Exits editing and restores the saved layout. Empty offers only Save as... and Discard changes ; the blank starting layout cannot be overwritten. Save as... suggests <model name>-L<number> , using the first unused number starting at 1, such as Sonic-L1 or My-Glider-L1 . You can change the suggestion using letters, digits, - , and _ (at most 24 characters). An existing name requires overwrite confirmation. Press RTN in the name dialog to return to the exit menu without losing your draft. After Save as..., restart the radio and select the new name in the widget's Layout setting. The dashboard continues showing its previous layout until you select the new one. Wait for saving to finish before powering off. A save error keeps your draft so you can retry. See Understand layouts for where saved layouts live and how multiple dashboards share them.

docs.text: Install and upgrade AeroGrid requires a color-screen radio running EdgeTX 2.11.0 or later. Install over USB below, or use manual installation . Your saved layouts, themes, and model settings in /AEROGRID/ stay in place. Back up your SD card before making changes. Both installation methods replace /WIDGETS/AeroGrid/ , discarding any files you added or changed there. The USB installer does not provide a backup or rollback; if replacement fails, retry the complete installation before using AeroGrid. If upgrading from a version that used /AEROGRID/registry.txt , rename it to layout-registry.txt before starting AeroGrid to preserve Layout selections. Do not edit or reorder its entries. Install over USB Use desktop Chrome or Edge . Power on the radio, connect its data USB port with a data cable, and choose USB Storage if prompted. Select Connect Radio below and choose the SD-card root: the folder containing RADIO , MODELS , and WIDGETS , not WIDGETS itself. Choose a release, review the compatibility message, and confirm installation. Latest stable is selected by default. Show developer releases includes the rolling development build; beta and RC releases require manual installation. docs.text: Edit model settings Watch the model settings walkthrough on YouTube . Long-press the AeroGrid dashboard to enter widget fullscreen. The AeroGrid icon appears in the top-left corner. Tap it, then choose Model settings . Settings apply to every AeroGrid dashboard for the selected model, not to an individual panel or layout. Each confirmed change saves automatically; Back closes the page. Chart recording time stops while this page is open and resumes with a pause gap. On EdgeTX 2.x, AeroGrid uses the CH32 name for its settings ID (for example, AGK7Q2 ). Leave that name unchanged; CH32's output limits are preserved. If CH32 already has another name, clear it before saving Model settings. New links and copied models are linked only while disarmed. Display-name changes keep the same settings. A copied model inherits settings when AeroGrid first loads it, then gets its own independent record. Model filename changes also create a new record; old records are left on the SD card. Changing or clearing the CH32 name unlinks settings; restoring the ID relinks them. The ID can appear in channel source lists and Output panels. To transfer settings to another radio, also copy /AEROGRID/models/<ID>.yaml from the SD card. Arming Arming tells AeroGrid when your model is armed, using the switch condition you select. It starts Chart recording, captures Navigation's first-arm home, and enables flight detection. It only observes your model's state; it does not arm the aircraft or control the motor. Setting Default What it does Arm switch None Physical switch position or logical switch (including inverted logical switches) that means armed. Saving None for Arm switch disables arming across all dashboards. Numeric sources such as ch5 or sa are not arm conditions. Flight detection Flight detection distinguishes a flight from simply being armed. It observes the armed condition, motor output, and (by default) live telemetry to confirm a flight start, then confirms its end after sustained disarming. Each confirmed start increments the model's flight total once, shown by Flight counter. Detection also supplies Chart flight shading, keeps recording running through the end-detection window, and drives the optional Flight status output for your sounds or announcements. It runs across the model's dashboards even without a Flight counter panel. Chart flight shading stays continuous if recording pauses during a flight. AeroGrid saves its own flight total per model and never writes GV8 or GV9. It keeps counting even when you display an external total. Setting Default What it does Motor channel CH3 Channel used to measure motor output. Reverse motor off Enable when the motor channel runs from high at idle to low at full power. Require receiver on Require a live receiver telemetry connection to confirm flight start. Turn off to test without a receiver; arming, motor threshold, and detection windows still apply. Motor threshold (%) 25 Motor output must be strictly above this percentage to qualify a flight. Set from 0 to 99 in whole-percent steps. Start detection window (s) 30 How long the start conditions must hold continuously to confirm flight start. End detection window (s) 10 Continuous disarming required to confirm flight end. Rearming within this window keeps the flight open. Smart detection off Also allows supported altitude or GPS groundspeed readings to confirm takeoff earlier. See Smart detection . Flight count source AeroGrid Show AeroGrid's total, GV9 in flight mode 0, or GV8:GV9 ( GV8 × 1000 + GV9 ) in flight mode 0. External GVs must have precision 0 and values from 0 to 999. On first setup, AeroGrid imports the total from a recognized Flights widget configured on the model's saved screens or top bar. It also imports compatible arming and detection settings if AeroGrid has none; review Model settings, especially for non-plane detection modes. Existing AeroGrid users retain their previous GV9 total. Without an existing counter, the total starts at zero. This import happens only once. Changing Flight count source only changes the displayed number; it never copies or resets either total. AeroGrid's detector still supplies the active-flight indication, so external and internal totals can differ. If you remove Flights, select AeroGrid to show the total AeroGrid has continued maintaining. Unavailable external data is reported rather than replaced with the internal total. Flight detection does not arm the aircraft. With Require receiver off, bench tests can increment the real flight total and activate the Flight status switch. Both detection windows can be set from 1 to 3600 seconds in whole-second steps. Flight timestamps use the beginning of each window, not the later confirmation. Interrupted start conditions restart the start window. A callback gap longer than a second restarts a pending start or end window rather than assuming the condition held. Smart detection Smart can confirm takeoff after more than 3 metres of altitude gain from the arming reference, or more than 10 mph GPS groundspeed , held for 2 seconds . Both paths still require arming, motor output above the threshold, and live telemetry when Require receiver is on. Supported CRSF/ELRS and FrSky S.Port sensors are discovered automatically. Model settings shows sensor readiness and any reason for falling back to standard detection. Missing, stale, or unsupported sensors never block the standard start window. Altitude requires a recent reading before or at the observed arm transition; opening AeroGrid already armed does not establish a reference. Smart is a takeoff aid, not a guarantee that every short hop will count or that fast taxiing will not count. Flight status output Flight status switch exposes the detected flight session through a dedicated Sticky logical switch. It turns on when flight start is confirmed and off when flight end is confirmed, including the end-detection window. Session reset also turns it off. Choose None to disable the output. For example, reserve an unused L01 in EdgeTX's Logical Switches page: Switch Function V1 V2 AND switch Delay Duration L01 Sticky unassigned unassigned unassigned 0.0 s 0.0 s Then select L01 as AeroGrid's Flight status switch . The picker lists configured logical switches. AeroGrid controls the switch's state; leave its inputs unassigned and reserve it exclusively for this output. Use L01 in an EdgeTX Special Function to play your chosen sound when a flight starts; use !L01 for an action when it ends. Configure the Special Function's startup and repeat options to avoid unwanted announcements. Do not also use this switch as the Arm switch or Session reset switch, or share it with another script. It is not a safety interlock: stopped scripts, model changes, and radio restarts cannot guarantee output cleanup. Session reset Set Session reset switch to a physical switch position or logical switch. Activation resets the following AeroGrid session data across all dashboards, including hidden screens: Panel or service What resets Chart Recordings, recorded extrema, flight shading, and arm/resume markers. Navigation First-arm captured home; a new disarm/arm transition is needed to capture again. RX battery Automatic cell estimate; fresh voltage supplies the next estimate. Flight counter / detection Pending or active detection and its flight-status output, not the flight total. Reset runs once per off-to-on transition, not continuously while held. An input already on at startup, after changing the setting, or after signal recovery does not trigger a reset. Choose None to disable it. Reset during a flight cancels detection without creating a completion. Disarm before another flight can be counted. Flight totals, radio timers, radio telemetry minima/maxima, EdgeTX home, saved settings/layouts, and unsaved editor changes are preserved. The dashboard stays on screen; only session-dependent content is redrawn. Pre-release features Pre-release features enables features that are not fully validated yet. It is a per-model setting that is off by default. EdgeTX stops a widget callback after 20,000 Lua instructions. docs.text: Watch the model settings walkthrough on YouTube . Long-press the AeroGrid dashboard to enter widget fullscreen. The AeroGrid icon appears in the top-left corner. Tap it, then choose Model settings . Settings apply to every AeroGrid dashboard for the selected model, not to an individual panel or layout. Each confirmed change saves automatically; Back closes the page. Chart recording time stops while this page is open and resumes with a pause gap. On EdgeTX 2.x, AeroGrid uses the CH32 name for its settings ID (for example, AGK7Q2 ). Leave that name unchanged; CH32's output limits are preserved. If CH32 already has another name, clear it before saving Model settings. New links and copied models are linked only while disarmed. Display-name changes keep the same settings. A copied model inherits settings when AeroGrid first loads it, then gets its own independent record. Model filename changes also create a new record; old records are left on the SD card. Changing or clearing the CH32 name unlinks settings; restoring the ID relinks them. The ID can appear in channel source lists and Output panels. To transfer settings to another radio, also copy /AEROGRID/models/<ID>.yaml from the SD card.
