docs.text: Arming tells AeroGrid when your model is armed, using the switch condition you select. It starts Chart recording, captures Navigation's first-arm home, and enables flight detection. It only observes your model's state; it does not arm the aircraft or control the motor. Setting Default What it does Arm switch None Physical switch position or logical switch (including inverted logical switches) that means armed. Saving None for Arm switch disables arming across all dashboards. Numeric sources such as ch5 or sa are not arm conditions.
docs.title: Arming

docs.text: Flight detection distinguishes a flight from simply being armed. It observes the armed condition, motor output, and (by default) live telemetry to confirm a flight start, then confirms its end after sustained disarming. Each confirmed start increments the model's flight total once, shown by Flight counter. Detection also supplies Chart flight shading, keeps recording running through the end-detection window, and drives the optional Flight status output for your sounds or announcements. It runs across the model's dashboards even without a Flight counter panel. Chart flight shading stays continuous if recording pauses during a flight. AeroGrid saves its own flight total per model and never writes GV8 or GV9. It keeps counting even when you display an external total. Setting Default What it does Motor channel CH3 Channel used to measure motor output. Reverse motor off Enable when the motor channel runs from high at idle to low at full power. Require receiver on Require a live receiver telemetry connection to confirm flight start. Turn off to test without a receiver; arming, motor threshold, and detection windows still apply. Motor threshold (%) 25 Motor output must be strictly above this percentage to qualify a flight. Set from 0 to 99 in whole-percent steps. Start detection window (s) 30 How long the start conditions must hold continuously to confirm flight start. End detection window (s) 10 Continuous disarming required to confirm flight end. Rearming within this window keeps the flight open. Smart detection off Also allows supported altitude or GPS groundspeed readings to confirm takeoff earlier. See Smart detection . Flight count source AeroGrid Show AeroGrid's total, GV9 in flight mode 0, or GV8:GV9 ( GV8 × 1000 + GV9 ) in flight mode 0. External GVs must have precision 0 and values from 0 to 999. On first setup, AeroGrid imports the total from a recognized Flights widget configured on the model's saved screens or top bar. It also imports compatible arming and detection settings if AeroGrid has none; review Model settings, especially for non-plane detection modes. Existing AeroGrid users retain their previous GV9 total. Without an existing counter, the total starts at zero. This import happens only once. Changing Flight count source only changes the displayed number; it never copies or resets either total. AeroGrid's detector still supplies the active-flight indication, so external and internal totals can differ. If you remove Flights, select AeroGrid to show the total AeroGrid has continued maintaining. Unavailable external data is reported rather than replaced with the internal total. Flight detection does not arm the aircraft. With Require receiver off, bench tests can increment the real flight total and activate the Flight status switch. Both detection windows can be set from 1 to 3600 seconds in whole-second steps. Flight timestamps use the beginning of each window, not the later confirmation. Interrupted start conditions restart the start window. A callback gap longer than a second restarts a pending start or end window rather than assuming the condition held.
docs.title: Flight detection

docs.text: Smart can confirm takeoff after more than 3 metres of altitude gain from the arming reference, or more than 10 mph GPS groundspeed , held for 2 seconds . Both paths still require arming, motor output above the threshold, and live telemetry when Require receiver is on. Supported CRSF/ELRS and FrSky S.Port sensors are discovered automatically. Model settings shows sensor readiness and any reason for falling back to standard detection. Missing, stale, or unsupported sensors never block the standard start window. Altitude requires a recent reading before or at the observed arm transition; opening AeroGrid already armed does not establish a reference. Smart is a takeoff aid, not a guarantee that every short hop will count or that fast taxiing will not count.

docs.text: Flight status switch exposes the detected flight session through a dedicated Sticky logical switch. It turns on when flight start is confirmed and off when flight end is confirmed, including the end-detection window. Session reset also turns it off. Choose None to disable the output. For example, reserve an unused L01 in EdgeTX's Logical Switches page: Switch Function V1 V2 AND switch Delay Duration L01 Sticky unassigned unassigned unassigned 0.0 s 0.0 s Then select L01 as AeroGrid's Flight status switch . The picker lists configured logical switches. AeroGrid controls the switch's state; leave its inputs unassigned and reserve it exclusively for this output. Use L01 in an EdgeTX Special Function to play your chosen sound when a flight starts; use !L01 for an action when it ends. Configure the Special Function's startup and repeat options to avoid unwanted announcements. Do not also use this switch as the Arm switch or Session reset switch, or share it with another script. It is not a safety interlock: stopped scripts, model changes, and radio restarts cannot guarantee output cleanup.

docs.text: Set Session reset switch to a physical switch position or logical switch. Activation resets the following AeroGrid session data across all dashboards, including hidden screens: Panel or service What resets Chart Recordings, recorded extrema, flight shading, and arm/resume markers. Navigation First-arm captured home; a new disarm/arm transition is needed to capture again. RX battery Automatic cell estimate; fresh voltage supplies the next estimate. Flight counter / detection Pending or active detection and its flight-status output, not the flight total. Reset runs once per off-to-on transition, not continuously while held. An input already on at startup, after changing the setting, or after signal recovery does not trigger a reset. Choose None to disable it. Reset during a flight cancels detection without creating a completion. Disarm before another flight can be counted. Flight totals, radio timers, radio telemetry minima/maxima, EdgeTX home, saved settings/layouts, and unsaved editor changes are preserved. The dashboard stays on screen; only session-dependent content is redrawn.

docs.text: Troubleshoot and file bugs Troubleshoot a reading If a panel shows no reading or an unexpected value: Open the panel's settings using its gear icon while editing. If it has a Source setting, check that you selected the value you want to display. For a telemetry reading, check that the receiver is connected and the sensor appears on the radio's Telemetry page. Check the guide for that panel for any additional setup: battery , timer , navigation , or metric . A missing reading does not mean the value is zero. Check layouts and themes The Diagnostics layout reports its own dashboard, not another dashboard's errors. To inspect a failing dashboard, add a Host diagnostics panel there and select panels . Use identity , theme , or sources to check its version, selected files, or source bindings. Check the selected Layout and Theme in the widget settings, and restart the radio or simulator after adding a new layout or theme. Saved files in /AEROGRID/layouts/ and /AEROGRID/themes/ override bundled files with the same name. Check whether an override explains an unexpected layout or color. See Add a dashboard and Customize themes for details. File a bug Search existing issues first. If none describes the problem, open a new issue . Include: Detail What to provide Summary What failed and a specific issue title. Versions AeroGrid package version or Git commit, EdgeTX version, and radio model. Environment Physical radio or simulator; simulator version and desktop OS when relevant. Reproduction Steps, selected layout and theme, and the smallest settings or layout that reproduce the problem. Expected and actual What should happen, what happens instead, and exact error text. Evidence Screenshots, recordings, or relevant diagnostics and logs. Data setup Sources, units, receiver/link state, switches, and timers needed to reproduce it. State whether the issue persists after a restart. Attach a minimal YAML layout, not an entire SD card. Remove private model information, GPS coordinates, and unrelated data before posting. For development-specific diagnostics and contribution guidance, see Issues, changes, and releases .
